decision.trend: Research on high-entropy alloys has focused on understanding their mechanical properties, such as strength, toughness, and fracture resistance. Earlier studies have explored the effects of composition, microstructure, and processing history on these properties. Recent studies have investigated the use of advanced characterization techniques, such as in situ straining and nanoindentation, to probe the atomistic to micro-scale mechanisms underlying the properties of high-entropy alloys. Additionally, researchers have explored the development of new high-entropy alloys with improved properties, such as enhanced toughness and strength, through the use of metastable particles, nano-bridged honeycomb microstructures, and controlled oxygen partial pressures.
decision.unsolved: Despite significant progress, the understanding of the relationships between composition, microstructure, and mechanical properties of high-entropy alloys remains incomplete. The development of high-entropy alloys with optimal combinations of strength, toughness, and fracture resistance remains a challenge. Furthermore, the effects of impurities, such as oxygen and nitrogen, on the long-term stability and mechanical properties of high-entropy alloys are not fully understood.
decision.why: To further understand the relationships between composition, microstructure, and mechanical properties of high-entropy alloys, and to develop new alloys with improved properties, it is necessary to employ advanced characterization techniques, such as nanoindentation and in situ straining, to probe the atomistic to micro-scale mechanisms underlying their properties. This will allow researchers to gain a deeper understanding of the deformation mechanisms and fracture behavior of high-entropy alloys, and to identify the key factors controlling their mechanical properties.
